Fold the four squares in the horizontal row as the four side faces of the cube. Take the square below the top square as the front face. Then:

- The top square becomes the top face. Its corner \(P\) folds to the back-top-left vertex of the cube.
- The leftmost square folds to the left side face. Its far top corner \(R\) also folds to the back-top-left vertex.
- \(S\) is the front-top-left vertex, and \(Q\) folds to a bottom-back vertex, so neither coincides with \(P\).

Therefore \(P\) occupies the same cube vertex as \(R\).
